## Subscription labels and observed token usage

This prerelease keeps the WebSocket/context safeguards from beta.1 and improves
how the dashboard reports upstream account metadata and recorded token usage.

- Preserve the upstream subscription identifier. Business Premium remains
  distinct from personal Pro 100; plan labels, search and sorting follow the
  [OpenAI Codex mapping](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/ca21fe65d18a9b6326759fb4263c65dfbb645aa5/codex-rs/tui/src/subscription.rs#L11-L39).
- Distinguish complete, partial and missing token observations across requests,
  conversations, accounts, API keys and dashboard totals. Incomplete totals use
  an exact lower bound (`>= N`); an actual measured zero remains zero. Historical
  rollups that did not retain completeness are explicitly marked unknown.
- Calculate total tokens as input plus output. Cached input is already part of
  input, and reasoning is already part of output. A reported reasoning count is
  used only as a lower bound when the full output count is absent.
- Settle API-key reservations for native failed/incomplete terminal responses
  when they report complete input/output usage, preserving idempotency and
  cancellation cleanup.
- Remove the synthetic Subscription balance derived from plan-capacity constants.
  Show reported quota percentages, reset times and purchased credits. Aggregate
  quota charts identify their equal-weight percentage average; unreported windows
  are excluded and a measured zero is included. Capacity forecasts remain labelled
  estimates.
- Display unavailable quota measurements explicitly, and explain when token
  observations and dashboard rows refresh.

## Scope

Counts cover observations recorded by this proxy. Missing terminal usage,
unseen retries and activity outside the proxy cannot be reconstructed. Compact
SSE failure/retry accounting is not completed by this release. Subscription
percentages do not reveal an exact remaining token allowance, and exact token
counts are available only after upstream reports usage.

Existing ambiguous `prolite` records are not rewritten as Business Premium;
an accepted upstream refresh can restore a more specific identifier. No database
migration or new configuration is required.

This release does not claim to resolve every WebSocket 1011/disconnection or
`Previous response was not found` error. It does not deploy or restart the
production server. The beta.1 tag and stable/latest images are preserved.

Publication targets GitHub, Docker (linux/amd64 and linux/arm64) and Helm.
Python distributions are attached to GitHub; PyPI upload is omitted.

Specifications and local regression evidence:
[observed token usage](https://github.com/Lok3rn3t/codexLB-up/tree/v1.26.0-beta.2/openspec/specs/observed-token-usage),
[quota presentation](https://github.com/Lok3rn3t/codexLB-up/tree/v1.26.0-beta.2/openspec/specs/account-quota-presentation).
